claims.text: A semiconducting SiGe-based nanocomposite can be used to study lattice heat conductivity.
Increasing the density of SRO precipitates in a SiGe-based nanocomposite will reduce its lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed SiGe-based nanocomposite is semiconducting.
The proposed material has a negligible free-carrier contribution to heat transport.
Negligible free-carrier heat transport causes lattice heat conduction to dominate in the proposed material.
The density and size of SRO precipitates can be introduced and systematically controlled within a SiGe matrix.
At room or moderate temperatures, phonon scattering is the dominant heat-transport mechanism in the proposed system.
SRO precipitates can be distributed uniformly within the SiGe matrix.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and scattering times lower lattice thermal conductivity.
A SiGe-based nanocomposite with a higher SRO-precipitate density will have measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than a comparable sample with few or no precipitates.
A pristine or minimally precipitated SiGe-based nanocomposite exhibits lattice-dominated thermal transport.
At higher temperatures or with increased electronic heat-transport contributions, the effect of SRO precipitates may be less clear.
The magnitude of the conductivity decrease requires experimental calibration.
A failure to observe a statistically significant conductivity decrease with increasing SRO-precipitate density would falsify the hypothesis.
